profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap point, labeled inforland.com with operator name inforland.com, carries coordinates placing it in or near Nerja, on the Costa del Sol in Malaga province, Spain. Despite the data center style tagging in source data, this registrys research this session could not confirm any real, currently operating business at this location under the name Inforland. The live inforland.com website was found to display only placeholder styled text reading InforLand.com on an otherwise blank page, along with a Tawk.to live chat widget script, with no company description, services list, address, or other content, and Wayback Machine archive records show only a single snapshot of the site, dated March 6, 2026, indicating little to no historical web footprint. A search for local Nerja area computer and IT businesses under similar names did not surface any confirmed match, and a separately named but apparently unrelated company, Inforland E.I.R.L., appears in Peru according to a business directory, with no evidence connecting it to this Spanish location or to the inforland.com domain. This registry records this honestly as an unverifiable or likely placeholder domain and location rather than fabricating a data center profile for it.

reading.body:
This entry documents a data center location that research could not verify as a real, operating facility.

The inforland.com domain and its associated OpenStreetMap point near Nerja, Spain show all the markers of a placeholder rather than an active business. The website contains only blank template text and a chat widget. Wayback Machine records a single snapshot from March 2026, indicating minimal historical presence. Local searches for matching businesses in the Nerja area found no confirmed operator.

The registry records this as an honest gap rather than fabricating details to fill it. No sources are cited because no sources actually confirmed a real facility here. The absence of verifiable information is itself the finding. This approach matters for infrastructure mapping: the grid and power constraints on AI scaling require identifying actual facilities, not domain registrations or placeholder entries.

What this entry does not tell readers is whether the location was ever intended as a data center, whether the domain represents abandoned plans, or how many similar unverifiable entries exist in broader infrastructure datasets. It demonstrates only that a single point in this registry could not be resolved to a confirmed operator or service.
